title: Graphs & Tables
sub: Reading bar graphs, tables and circle graphs

steps.html:
Graphs & Tables

Votes for team color

total = 12 + 20 + 8 + 10 = 50
fraction for Red = 1250 = 625
say: Today: reading graphs. This bar graph shows votes for a team color.
What fraction went to Red? Red is twelve, but the bottom of the fraction is all the votes: twelve plus twenty plus eight plus ten, fifty. So twelve fiftieths, or six twenty-fifths.

steps.html:
Read carefully

Read the labelstitle, axis, units (thousands? %?)
“Of all” → totaladd every bar for the bottom
Percent changechange ÷ the starting value
say: Read the labels first: the title, the axes, and the units.
When they say of all, you need the total of every bar.
And for percent change, divide the change by the starting value.

steps.html: Shirts sold: Week 1: 120, Week 2: 96. By what percent did sales decrease?
say: Shirts sold were one twenty in week one and ninety-six in week two. By what percent did sales decrease?
steps.okSay: Yes! A drop of twenty-four out of one twenty is twenty percent.
steps.no: Change = 120 − 96 = 24. Divide by the start: 24120 = 0.2 = 20%. (24 ÷ 96 = 25% uses the wrong base.)
steps.noSay: Not quite. The drop is twenty-four. Divide by the starting value, one twenty: twenty percent.

steps.html:
Circle graphs

200 students, 20% chose swimming
20% of 200 = 40 students

A whole circle = 100% = 360°.
say: Circle graphs show parts of a whole, usually as percents.
Two hundred students, and twenty percent chose swimming.
Twenty percent of two hundred is forty students.
Remember, the whole circle is one hundred percent, or three hundred sixty degrees.
Great! Now 4 practice questions. You'll see the answer and an explanation after each one.
Last part: three checkpoint questions. Get two out of three to finish the lesson. You've got this!

steps.html:
Remember

1. Read the title, axes and units first.

2. “Of all” → add everything for the total.

3. Percent change: ÷ the starting value.

4. Circle graph: whole = 100% = 360°.
say: Let's review. Read the title, axes, and units first.
Of all means use the total of everything.
Percent change divides by the starting value.
And a circle graph's whole is one hundred percent, or three sixty degrees. Great job!
